JOE

TD King 21 → Krumb Lord → Thielen my Chubb → The Bye Week

Two rings, fourteen years apart, with two straight gut-punch finals losses right before the second one. Also owns the single highest-scoring week ever played.

2 Rings · 246.70 Record

BOB

The Snozzberries

Seventeen playoff trips in nineteen seasons. The best career win percentage in the league. The guy you forget is good until he's beating you in Week 14.

2 Rings · 17/19 Playoffs

GATI

Eleven team names and counting

Harry Plopper. Gangsta Panda. Sex Panther. Fat Ewoks. A different identity almost every year — and somehow two championships buried in there.

2 Rings · 11 Alter Egos

SCOTT

Chemical Toilet → I Like Turtles

The most championships in league history — four rings — and a career losing record. Went 1-12 the year after a title. Did it again eight years later. Rebuilt into a champion both times.

4 Rings · Boom or Bust

BILL

Max Bet · League Commissioner

Writes the rules. Has the worst career win percentage of any multi-time champion in the league. Somehow still has two rings. Draw your own conclusions.

2 Rings · The Commish

RICH

Dream Team2 → Eagles Rock 2

Joined the league a decade late. Won the title in his first season anyway. Three rings in nine years — the best rate of return anyone has ever posted.

3 Rings · Instant Impact

CHRIS

Cheesesteak's — never once rebranded

Went 1-12 in 2020. Never changed the name. Won the whole thing five years later. The longest doormat-to-champion turnaround in league history.

1 Ring · Never Wavered

SEAN

Virginia Eagles

Six playoff trips in eight years. A winning record. One runner-up finish. Zero rings. The most reliable manager in the league who has never once closed it out.

0 Rings · Always Close

DREW

Chemical Toilet → Stu Pedasso

Inherited a franchise fresh off a 1-13 season, made the playoffs with it, then fled to a brand new team name that promptly went 3-11. There's a curse here somewhere.

Hawk Time

Made the championship game in his very first season in the league. Followed it up with two years of near-last-place finishes. The sophomore slump that lasted two extra years. Nobody has a photo of him because he has never once shown up to the draft — at this point some managers consider him a myth.
